title: Iconography / Expressive pictogram vocabulary

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Expressive

slide_intent: Choose stronger visual presence deliberately, because expressive detail can attract attention but may be unnecessary for a simple functional action.
strategic_value: A shared combination of thin black detail and blue-violet gradient strokes can make IBM’s expressive symbols recognizable as a family.
demonstration: Eighteen expressive pictograms occupy a three-row, six-column grid under the selected Expressive tab, showing people, networks, data, shopping and other concepts.
practical_value: Compare the expressive vocabulary before selecting a pictogram for a context that warrants visual emphasis.

content_islands.name: Specimen grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange the eighteen symbols in equal cells, preserving their mix of black detail, circular points and colored gradient paths.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying overview explains that expressive pictograms are for selected uses needing greater visual impact.
reference_purposes.Expression: The repeated stroke, point and gradient treatments unite the varied concepts into a recognizable style.
reference_purposes.Application: The specimen set makes the expressive option available for comparison with the productive type in the parent page.
